questions.text: A layer-4 firewall (a device that can look at all protocol headers up to the transport layer) CANNOT
questions.optA: block entire HTTP traffic during 9:00 pm and 5:00 am

questions.text: If two fair coins are flipped and at least one of the outcomes is known to be a head, what is the probability that both outcomes are heads?
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: With two independent fair coins, the equally likely outcomes remaining after excluding TT are HH, HT and TH. Only HH satisfies both heads, so the conditional probability is 1/3.

questions.text:
A company needs to develop a strategy for software product development for which it has a choice of two programming languages L1 and L2. The number of lines of code (LOC) developed using L2 is estimated to be twice the LOC developed with L1. The product will have to be maintained for five years. Various parameters for the company are given in the table below.
$$\begin{array}{l|c|c}\text{Parameter}&\text{Language L1}&\text{Language L2}\\\hline\text{Man years needed for development}&\mathrm{LOC}/10000&\mathrm{LOC}/10000\\\text{Development Cost per man year}&\text{Rs. 10,00,000}&\text{Rs. 7,50,000}\\\text{Maintenance time}&\text{5 years}&\text{5 years}\\\text{Cost of maintenance per year}&\text{Rs. 1,00,000}&\text{Rs. 50,000}\end{array}$$
Total cost of the project includes cost of development and maintenance. What is the LOC for L1 for which the cost of the project using L1 is equal to the cost of the project using L2?
questions.referenceAnswer: Let $x$ be L1 LOC; L2 then has $2x$ LOC. In rupees, L1 costs $100x+500000$ and L2 costs $150x+250000$. Equating gives $50x=250000$, hence $x=5000$. The annual maintenance cost is multiplied by five in both cases.

questions.text: Let the time taken to switch between user and Kernel modes of execution be $t_1$ while the time taken to switch between two processes be $t_2$. Which of the following is TRUE?
questions.rawTopic: Process Management-I (Introduction, Process, Threads & CPU Scheduling)
questions.optD: nothing can be said about the relation between $t_1$ and $t_2$
questions.subject: 5. Operating Systems
questions.referenceAnswer: A user/kernel mode switch changes privilege and execution mode. A process context switch additionally saves/restores process state and may switch address space, so the conventional comparison is t1 < t2.

notes: Answer transcribed from the printed chapter key, PDF page 5 / book page 533.

questions.text: A company needs to develop digital signal processing software for one of its newest inventions. The software is expected to have 40000 lines of code. The company needs to determine the effort in person-months needed to develop this software using the basic COCOMO model. The multiplicative factor for this model is given as 2.8 for the software development on embedded systems, while the exponentiation factor is given as 1.20. What is the estimated effort in person-months?
questions.referenceAnswer: COCOMO uses thousands of delivered source lines: KLOC = 40. Effort $=2.8(40)^{1.20}=234.22326\ldots$ person-months, closest to 234.25.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs have DIFFERENT expressive power?
questions.optA: Deterministic finite automata (DFA) and Non-deterministic finite automata (NFA)
questions.optB: Deterministic push down automata (DPDA) and Non-deterministic push down automata (NPDA)
questions.optC: Deterministic single-tape Turing machine and Non-deterministic single-tape Turing machine
questions.optD: Single-tape Turing machine and multi-tape Turing machine
questions.referenceAnswer: DFAs and NFAs recognize the same regular languages. Deterministic and nondeterministic Turing machines, and one-tape and multi-tape machines, have the same language-recognition power. Deterministic pushdown automata recognize a strict subset of the context-free languages recognized by nondeterministic PDAs.

questions.text: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) has language elements which permit certain actions other than describing the structure of the web document. Which one of the following actions is NOT supported by pure HTML (without any server or client side scripting) pages?
questions.optA: Embed web objects from different sites into the same page
questions.optB: Refresh the page automatically after a specified interval
questions.optC: Automatically redirect to another page upon download
questions.optD: Display the client time as part of the page
questions.referenceAnswer: Static HTML can embed objects, and refresh metadata can request timed refresh or redirection. Reading and displaying the current client clock needs executable client-side behavior rather than pure HTML.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT desired in a good Software Requirement Specifications (SRS) document?
questions.referenceAnswer: An SRS specifies the required externally observable behavior, constraints and quality requirements. Algorithms for implementing the software are design/implementation decisions, rather than requirements.

questions.text:
A computer handles several interrupt sources of which the following are relevant for this question.
• Interrupt from CPU temperature sensor (raises interrupt if CPU temperature is too high)
• Interrupt from Mouse (raises interrupt if the mouse is moved or a button is pressed)
• Interrupt from Keyboard (raises interrupt when a key is pressed or released)
• Interrupt from Hard Disk (raises interrupt when a disk read is completed)
Which one of these will be handled at the HIGHEST priority?
questions.rawTopic: Process Management-I (Introduction, Process, Threads & CPU Scheduling)
questions.subject: 5. Operating Systems
questions.referenceAnswer: The overheating interrupt protects the processor from physical damage and must take priority over ordinary disk, mouse and keyboard service. The answer concerns the stated safety event rather than a universal fixed priority among peripheral devices.

notes: Answer transcribed from the printed chapter key, PDF page 5 / book page 533.

questions.text:
Consider a relational table with a single record for each registered student with the following attributes.
1. Registration_Num: Unique registration number of each registered student
2. UID: Unique identity number, unique at the national level for each citizen
3. BankAccount_Num: Unique account number at the bank. A student can have multiple accounts or joint accounts. This attribute stores the primary account number
4. Name: Name of the student
5. Hostel_Room: Room number of the hostel
Which of the following options is INCORRECT?
questions.optB: Registration_Num can be a primary key
questions.optC: UID is a candidate key if all students are from the same country
questions.optD: If S is a superkey such that $S\cap\text{UID}$ is NULL then $S\cup\text{UID}$ is also a superkey
questions.subject: 12. DBMS
questions.referenceAnswer: An account may be jointly held, so the primary bank-account number need not uniquely identify a student and is not necessarily a candidate key. Registration number is unique. A national UID is unique when all students share a country. Adding attributes to a superkey preserves its superkey property.

questions.text: A thread is usually defined as a "light weight process" because an Operating System (OS) maintains smaller data structures for a thread than for a process. In relation to this, which of the following is TRUE?
questions.rawTopic: Process Management-I (Introduction, Process, Threads & CPU Scheduling)
questions.optA: On per-thread basis, the OS maintains only CPU register state
questions.optB: The OS does not maintain a separate stack for each thread
questions.optC: On per-thread basis, the OS does not maintain virtual memory state
questions.optD: On per-thread basis, the OS maintains only scheduling and accounting information
questions.subject: 5. Operating Systems
questions.referenceAnswer: Threads of a process share its virtual address space. Each thread still needs its own stack, register state and scheduling information, but the OS does not maintain a separate virtual-memory state for each thread.

questions.text: If the difference between the expectation of the square of a random variable $(\mathrm{E}[x^2])$ and the square of the expectation of the random variable $(\mathrm{E}[x])^2$ is denoted by $R$, then
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: The difference is $R=\mathrm E[X^2]-(\mathrm E[X])^2=\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathrm E[(X-\mathrm E[X])^2]\ge0$. It can equal zero for a constant random variable, so strict positivity is not guaranteed.

questions.text: The lexical analysis for a modern computer language such as Java needs the power of which one of the following machine models in a necessary and sufficient sense?
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: Lexical patterns form regular languages and can be recognized by finite-state automata. A stack or unrestricted tape is unnecessary for this lexical phase; syntactic analysis is a different task.

questions.text: Let the page fault service time be 10 ms in a computer with average memory access time being 20 ns. If one page fault is generated for every $10^6$ memory accesses, what is the effective access time for the memory?
questions.subject: 5. Operating Systems
questions.referenceAnswer: The fault probability is $10^{-6}$ and 10 ms is $10^7$ ns. Effective access time is $(1-10^{-6})20+10^{-6}(10^7)=29.99998$ ns, approximately 30 ns. Adding the ordinary access after fault service changes only an insignificant fraction here.

questions.text: Consider a hypothetical processor with a instruction of type LW R1, 20(R2), which during execution reads a 32-bit word from memory and stores it in a 32-bit register R1. The effective address of the memory location is obtained by the addition of a constant 20 and the contents of register R2. Which of the following best reflects the addressing mode implemented by this instruction for the operand in memory?
questions.subject: 4. COA
questions.referenceAnswer: The effective address is contents(R2) + 20. This is a base-register plus displacement address; among the offered names, Base Indexed Addressing (D) is the intended match. It is neither an immediate operand nor a scaled register index.

questions.text: Let P be a regular language and Q be a context-free language such that $Q \subseteq P$. (For example, let P be the language represented by the regular expression $p^*q^*$ and Q be $\{p^nq^n \mid n \in \mathbb{N}\}$). Then which of the following is ALWAYS regular?
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: Regular languages are closed under complement, so $\Sigma^*-P$ is always regular. Choosing $P=p^*q^*$ and $Q=\{p^nq^n\}$ shows the other operations need not preserve regularity.

questions.text:
An algorithm to find the length of the longest monotonically increasing sequence of numbers in an array $A[0:n-1]$ is given below.
Let $L_i$ denotes the length of the longest monotonically increasing sequence starting at index $i$ in the array
Initialize $L_{n-1}=1$
For all $i$ such that $0\le i\le n-2$
$$L_i=\begin{cases}1+L_{i+1}, & \text{If }A[i]<A[i+1]\\1, & \text{Otherwise}\end{cases}$$
Finally the length of the longest monotonically increasing sequence is $\operatorname{Max}(L_0,L_1,\ldots,L_{n-1})$.
Which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.optA: The algorithm uses dynamic programming paradigm
questions.optB: The algorithm has a linear complexity and uses branch and bound paradigm
questions.optC: The algorithm has a non-linear polynomial complexity and uses branch and bound paradigm
questions.optD: The algorithm uses divide and conquer paradigm
questions.subject: 7. Algorithms
questions.referenceAnswer: The recurrence reuses the previously computed value at the next index, which is dynamic programming. A reverse traversal computes all values in linear time. The displayed recurrence actually describes a contiguous increasing run rather than an arbitrary increasing subsequence, and the source does not specify traversal order; these wording defects do not change the paradigm choice A. The final bound is Ln-1 in this scan, not the book copy Ln+1.

questions.text:
Consider the languages L1, L2 and L3 as given below 
$L1=\{0^{p}1^{q}|p,q\in N\}$
$ L2=\{0^{p}1^{q}|p,q\in N and p=q\} $ and 
$L3=\{0^{p}1^{q}0^{r}|p,q,r\in N \; and \; p=q=r\}$ 
Which of the following statements is NOT TRUE?
questions.optA: Push Down Automata (PDA) can be used to recognize L1 and L2
questions.optC: All the three languages are context free
questions.optD: Turing machines can be used to recognize all the languages
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: L1 is regular and L2 is context-free, so both are recognized by PDAs. L3 requires equality of all three block lengths and is not context-free. All are decidable by Turing machines. Thus the claim that all three are context-free is false.

questions.text: Consider two binary operators '$\uparrow$' and '$\downarrow$' with the precedence of operator $\downarrow$ being lower than that of the operator $\uparrow$. Operator $\uparrow$ is right associative while operator $\downarrow$ is left associative. Which one of the following represents the parse tree for expression $(7\downarrow3\uparrow4\uparrow3\downarrow2)$

questions.referenceAnswer: Higher-precedence up arrows group first, and their right associativity gives $3\uparrow(4\uparrow3)$. The down arrows then associate left, producing $(7\downarrow(3\uparrow(4\uparrow3)))\downarrow2$. This is tree B.

questions.text:
Which one of the following options is CORRECT given three positive integers $x, y$ and $z$, and a predicate
$P(x) = \neg (x = 1) \wedge \forall y (\exists z (x = y * z) \Rightarrow (y = x) \vee (y = 1))$
questions.optA: $P(x)$ being true means that $x$ is a prime number
questions.optB: $P(x)$ being true means that $x$ is a number other than 1
questions.optC: $P(x)$ is always true irrespective of the value of $x$
questions.optD: $P(x)$ being true means that $x$ has exactly two factors other than 1 and $x$
questions.subject: 1. Discrete Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: The predicate excludes x=1 and states that every positive divisor y of x is either 1 or x. This is precisely the definition of a prime positive integer.

questions.text: Given $i=\sqrt{-1}$, what will be the evaluation of the definite integral $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\dfrac{\cos x+i\sin x}{\cos x-i\sin x}\,dx$?
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: The quotient is $e^{ix}/e^{-ix}=e^{2ix}$. Therefore the integral is $[e^{2ix}/(2i)]_0^{\pi/2}=(-1-1)/(2i)=i$.

questions.text:
Consider a database table T containing two columns X and Y each of type integer. After the creation of the table, one record $(X=1,Y=1)$ is inserted in the table.
Let MX and MY denote the respective maximum values of X and Y among all records in the table at any point in time. Using MX and MY, new records are inserted in the table 128 times with X and Y values being $MX+1$, $2*MY+1$ respectively. It may be noted that each time after the insertion, values of MX and MY change.
What will be the output of the following SQL query after the steps mentioned above are carried out?
[CODE]
questions.code: SELECT Y FROM T WHERE X = 7;
questions.subject: 12. DBMS
questions.referenceAnswer: The inserted rows satisfy $X=k$, $Y=2^k-1$, beginning at (1,1). Thus at X=7, Y=$2^7-1=127$. Later insertions do not modify that row.

questions.text: Consider the finite sequence of random values $X=[x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_n]$. Let $\mu_x$ be the mean and $\sigma_x$ be the standard deviation of $X$. Let another finite sequence $Y$ of equal length be derived from this as $y_i=a*x_i+b$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. Let $\mu_y$ be the mean and $\sigma_y$ be the standard deviation of this sequence. Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
questions.optA: Index position of mode of $X$ in $X$ is the same as the index position of mode of $Y$ in $Y$.
questions.optB: Index position of median of $X$ in $X$ is the same as the index position of median of $Y$ in $Y$.
questions.subject: 11. Engg. Maths
questions.referenceAnswer: For positive a, the affine map preserves order and equal-value groups, and $\mu_y=a\mu_x+b$. Standard deviation is $\sigma_y=a\sigma_x$; adding b does not change deviations from the mean. Hence D is incorrect.

questions.text: A deck of 5 cards (each carrying a distinct number from 1 to 5) is shuffled thoroughly. Two cards are then removed one at a time from the deck. questions.text: Definition of a language L with alphabet $\{a\}$ is given as follows: $L = \{a^{nk} \mid k > 0, \text{ and } n \text{ is a positive integer constant}\}$. What is the minimum number of states needed in a dfa to recognize L?
questions.subject: 2. TOC
questions.referenceAnswer: Positive multiples of n are accepted, but the empty string is rejected. A cycle of n residue states plus a distinct rejecting start state recognizes the language. Each distance vector is the distance of the best known path at that instance to nodes, N1 to N5, where the distance to itself is 0. Each distance vector is the distance of the best known path at that instance to nodes, N1 to N5, where the distance to itself is 0. questions.text: The variable cost (V) of manufacturing a product varies according to the equation $V=4q$, where $q$ is the quantity produced. The fixed cost (F) of production of same product reduces with $q$ according to the equation $F=100/q$. How many units should be produced to minimize the total cost $(V+F)$?
questions.referenceAnswer: Total cost is $C(q)=4q+100/q$ for q>0. Its derivative is $4-100/q^2$, zero at q=5. Since $C''(q)=200/q^3>0$, this is the unique minimum, including among the offered positive integers.

questions.text: A transporter receives the same number of orders each day. Currently, he has some pending orders (backlog) to be shipped. If he uses 7 trucks, then at the end of the 4th day he can clear all the orders. Alternatively, if he uses only 3 trucks, then all the orders are cleared at the end of the 10th day. What is the minimum number of trucks required so that there will be no pending order at the end of the 5th day?
questions.referenceAnswer: Measure work in one truck-day. With backlog B and daily arrivals a, $B+4a=28$ and $B+10a=30$. Hence $a=1/3$ and $B=80/3$. Work through day five is $85/3$ truck-days, requiring $17/3$ trucks; the least integer is six.

questions.text: A container originally contains 10 litres of pure spirit. From this container 1 litre of spirit is replaced with 1 litre of water. Subsequently 1 litre of the mixture is again replaced with 1 litre of water and this process is repeated one more time. How much spirit is now left in the container?
